hook_text: A hole is round. From the side it is two dashed lines. Both are true, and that is the whole trick of orthographic drawing.
clip_script: Take a block with a chamfered edge and a bolt hole. The chamfer shows its real 45 degrees in one view only, the one looking along it; elsewhere it is a flat strip. The hole is a circle with crossed centre lines from above, and from the front and side it is two dashed lines a hole's width apart, because you are looking across a tube, not down it. Rule: a feature is true in the view that looks at it square-on and becomes lines everywhere else, dashed if hidden. Tools keep it honest: 45 set square for the chamfer and the mitre line, compass set to the radius, hard pencil feint and soft pencil dark. Then the reverse game: three views given, trace every feature through all three, and the solid appears in your head.
visual_style: Whiteboard block rotating to three flat views; a hole becoming a circle then dashed lines; a 45 degree mitre line carrying a depth round the corner.
pacing: Chamfer, hole, rule, tools, reverse game.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the three views of a mug with its handle hidden.
